verdicts.reason: Same correct ₹394 unit economics and ad-set P&L in both, but Output 2 also catches that the current ₹44,900/day run rate overshoots the ₹12 lakh monthly budget, sets a midpoint working target, and adds refusal-rate-by-ad-set and GST checks; Output 1 is more decisive on cutting Razor Starter.

Both have correct $27.10 break-even and $38 parity logic; Output 1 is more Monday-ready with owner/done-when setup steps, a launch gate, explicit creator disclosure and marginal-cost-after-raise rule, while Output 2's blended lift check is good but its rules are a bit looser.

Output 1 gives eight sharply distinct concepts with headlines, safe zones and a concrete keep/cut rule, and stays strictly within approved claims; Output 2's cost-per-trip ad implies durability ('every year after that is extra') beyond the approved specs and its test plan is vaguer.

Output 1's creator brief is fuller (spoken plus on-screen disclosure, usage rights, fees, dates, deliverables) and its angles are more distinct; Output 2 is clean and compliant but lacks rights/timeline and its creator brief is thinner.

Both are within limits and claim-safe; Output 2's angles and descriptions vary more (Output 1 repeats the price in every primary text) and its compliance checklist is tighter, though Output 1's FSSAI check is a good touch.

Near-identical copy, but Output 2 builds the note-count fix into the spec and FAQ and redirects cash-heavy buyers to a full-note wallet range, keeping the sale instead of losing it, with a fallback if conversion drops.

Output 1 has tighter Klaviyo mechanics (unique coupon tag, checkout-pause, opt-in-only WhatsApp with quick-reply skin-type buttons) and A/B subjects; Output 2 is solid and adds a holdout but leans on a shared static code and a plain reminder WhatsApp.

Output 1 protects margin by holding offers to message 3, segmenting by value and discount history, giving no discount to the over-365 group and sizing holdout precision correctly; Output 2's math checks out but it hands 15% to every deep-lapsed customer up front, leaking discount to people who would return anyway.

Both find the $71.44 vs $104 first-order loss, but Output 2 translates every move into contribution margin as a share of revenue (13.6% to 7.8%, each $10 of CAC = 2.9%), all of which check out and speak directly to the board's margin goal; Output 1 mixes per-1,000 units and adds an invented '300 screen'.

Both have correct bundle and threshold math, but Output 2 uses a more cautious top-up assumption, compares ₹699 against ₹849, sets a cannibalisation break-even for the Duo, counts COD only when delivered and flags the ASCI 'free' rule; Output 1 rests on an optimistic 40% top-up share.

Both size MDEs correctly; Output 1 is faster with a clever 2x2, but Output 2 judges every test on orders per visitor rather than add-to-cart, measures the EMI/COD test on delivered orders, and tracks trial returns before keeping a win.

Output 1 sizes the prepaid nudge at ₹20 because confirmation itself cuts RTO savings to about ₹22, skips confirming proven COD buyers, sizes call capacity and adds a cart holdout; Output 2 leaves offers and policies as placeholders and adds a second cart discount that costs margin.
